summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to discuss phases 42–44 of the cipher-box project (IPFS unpin integrity, FUSE write durability, IPNS conflict handling) and then plan phase 42.
summary.outcome: All three phases were fully discussed with CONTEXT.md, DISCUSSION-LOG.md, and checkpoint files committed. Phase 42 was planned end-to-end, producing 3 PLAN files, PATTERNS.md, and VALIDATION.md after recovering from a mid-run planner failure.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) has no ownership check — only JwtAuthGuard, so any authenticated user can destroy another user's pinned content with their own JWT.

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile in staging, exposing swarm port 4001 publicly and participating in the public DHT — all pinned CIDs are harvestable by crawlers even though blob content is encrypted.
Kubo API port 5001 is loopback-only since Phase 29; the NestJS API endpoint is the sole public path into Kubo.
IPFS content-addressed dedup means multiple users can reference the same CID, making refcount logic required before issuing pin/rm.
Current callers ignore unpin errors silently: web uses .catch(logger.warn), FUSE uses let _ =, so any status-code change is a forward-looking API contract decision rather than a behavioral fix.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts), so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path today.
eslint already ignores .planning and .claude directories; .prettierignore was absent and needed to be created to protect markdown plans.
The BYO (bring-your-own IPFS) capability injects its own pinFn and does not go through the managed Kubo unpin path.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm on a CID that may be content-addressed shared with another user, creating a cross-tenant data-destruction vector
Kubo v0.40 uses 'server' profile with swarm port 4001 exposed publicly — full DHT participation means pinned CIDs are advertised as provider records and harvestable at scale
FUSE write path has a durability gap: data loss is possible before remote commit on release, and mkdir parent-publish can create orphaned directory entries
SDK queue facility available as the durability primitive for the FUSE write-path fix in phase 43
Folder IPNS write path inspected for phase 44 conflict-handling decisions — IPNS write auth is cryptographic, bounding the conflict surface

workflow: GSD manager runs plan and discuss as inline Skill calls on Claude Code (not background agents) so plan-checker, worktree isolation, and quality gates actually execute.
Prettier treats pipe characters in markdown as table column separators, corrupting test command regexes in VALIDATION.md — .prettierignore must cover .planning from project inception.
When a planning agent dies mid-run, checking plan file tail completeness and spawning a targeted completion agent is an effective recovery pattern without full replan.
Phase commits should be verified with git log immediately — phase 44's first commit silently failed and required investigation and retry.

friction: Session limit hit mid-discussion of phase 42, interrupting the flow before area 1 was locked.
Phase 44 commit did not land on the first attempt — git log still showed phase 43 as HEAD, requiring explicit diagnosis and retry.
Prettier mangled a test command regex in 42-VALIDATION.md by interpreting the pipe as a table column separator; required an Edit fix and adding .prettierignore.
The plan agent for phase 42 died partway through, leaving incomplete PLAN files; a separate completion agent was needed to recover.
The discuss workflow defaulted to presenting option menus instead of answering the user's direct questions; required explicit user feedback to change approach.
open_items: BYO (bring-your-own IPFS) unpin path not wired into delete flows — explicitly deferred out of phase 42 scope.
Drift-detection job (read-only pin ls diff against pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins) deferred as defense-in-depth, not a phase 42 deliverable.
Phases 43 (FUSE write durability) and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) are discussed but not yet planned.
Per-CID Postgres advisory lock on hash(cid) to close the concurrent-unpin refcount race must be implemented in phase 42 execution.
Pending-unpins outbox pattern (transactional insert on last-reference delete, Kubo pin/rm on drain) must be implemented so Kubo state is recoverable after crashes.
